Yadin: A proactive kid and a forward-thinking man. Set-backs, yep, we all have them, but sadly few of us realise they’re actually springboards to greatness, for later on. It’s just how it is and Yadin is all over it.
Yadran: To suggest Yadran is calculated is to do the man a disservice. Yes, he's a staunch competitor and he hates, hates, hates coming last, but a sense of humour is never far away. For example, having not sat over a chess board for 15 years or so, he is the sort of fellow who, when asked out of the blue by a young nephew if he'd like a game, is not only delighted at seeing first-hand how a young man he loves is progressing, he will be flooded with the glorious memories of what playing chess does to his brain. Most notably, it's the hidden strategy that he missed (which, to a lesser extent he's applied to his own life) and the notion of cornering your opposition through a greater intelligence. (In reality, of course, he'll let his nephew beat him every third game.)
Yang: Chinese herbalist. No matter what ailment he's told of and no matter how grim the forecast for a person, you'll rarely see him without a smile. Everything is connected, he'll tell you. Everything.
Yanni: My god, what a great big dollop of over-the-top romantic fluff and carry-on is he. Yanni, why didn’t you ever get yourself off to acting school? Although it’s never too late, eh?
Yannis: A big, hairy Greek man whose eyebrows have melded into one giant, black snake. He's as soft and as cuddly as a seven foot toy teddy bear.
Yash:
The fridge stopped working? The dingy sprung a leak? The fan belt broke out in the middle of nowhere?
Fear not. Yash will leap into action, making a joke at every turn while he does his darndest to fix the problem, usually employing completely unorthodox methodology. 
Success rate: 78% 
(as opposed to his romantic success rate: 83%)
Yens: Is Yens a dishwasher technician with a German heritage? Well, certainly, of all the people in the Kingdom who could perform at this job admirably there are very few out there who could do it better. No, he doesn’t laugh at meaningless jokes but he is a fabulous, upstanding, loyal man and he oozes technical competence no matter what he’s into. Not a fingernail biter. Yens.
Yoey:
Yoey approaches life like a skimming stone that is 4-bounces into a perfect 9-bounce performance. 
Question: What’s possible?
Answer:  Everything.
Yogi: ……..suuuuuuuuure, he is! He's not that deep.
Yong: Yong performs autopsies in the name of forensic science.
Yoshi: Yoshi is something of a marvel. If a moment of possible humour and love presents itself Yoshi acts without thinking and the results are stupendous. It's a lesson for each of us, actually.
Yossi: Where do you begin? What could take hours we’ll boil down to this: Give him his violin or his grand piano (a good one), or whatever musical/creative medium blows his hair back, stand back and just let him do his thing. He loves what he does and tears of joy have been known to be shed by onlookers.
Youcef: If you think Youcef is useless you can leave the room for he is a dedicated, animated liver of life whose courage and honour could teach many within the Kingdom a valuable lesson or two. His only real fault, if you can call it that, is that he might occasionally smother people with love.
Youssef: Youssef is a staunch-but-fair competitor. Never effusive, well, unless he is watching his son or daughter play soccer, Youssef is a friendly and committed chump who gallops through life with a smile stuck to the front of his head. He only frowns if, and when, people don’t do what they say they are going to do. Youssef commits and he expects you to commit as well. The End.
Yuri: The textbook Russian spy. Very intelligent and with a high tolerance to pain, Yuri is a very direct person. Fascinating too, once you get to know him, and entertaining for that matter. Indeed, Yuri is good value, just make sure you read the “Safe Handling Methods” handbook for Yuri, beforehand.
